issue.title: 404 for an unknown "auto/…" model reports a synthesized id ("group/auto-deepseek-v4-1-flash") instead of the id the client sent
issue.body:
### What happens

An unknown model id that starts with `auto/` makes the gateway report a **synthesized internal id** that the client never sent:

```
POST /v1/chat/completions   {"model": "auto/deepseek-v4.1-flash", ...}
→ 404  magpie knows no model "group/auto-deepseek-v4-1-flash"; did you mean
       workbuddy-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash, opencode-zen-free/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free,
       openrouter/minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash:free?
```

The client sent `auto/deepseek-v4.1-flash`; the message talks about `group/auto-deepseek-v4-1-flash` — a different string, with the dots rewritten to dashes and a `group/` prefix. That id exists nowhere: it is not in `GET /v1/models`, not in `magpie groups`, and cannot be searched or copied back.

### Why it is inconsistent

| request `model` | 404 message names |
|---|---|
| `auto/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `group/auto-deepseek-v4-1-flash` ← synthesized |
| `auto/nope-model` | `group/auto-nope-model` ← synthesized |
| `nosuchgroup/foo` | `nosuchgroup/foo` ← echoed verbatim |
| `magpie/workbuddy-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `magpie/workbuddy-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash` ← echoed verbatim |

So only the `auto/…` path leaks an internal key; every other unknown id is echoed as sent.

### Environment

- magpie `0.1.1296` (Windows 11, gateway on `127.0.0.1:3425`)
- `magpie groups` on this machine lists exactly one auto group: `auto/step-5-preview` (smart, `workbuddy/step-5-preview · workbuddy-ai/step-5-preview`)

### Repro

```bash
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"auto/deepseek-v4.1-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":8}'
```

### Expected

One of:

- echo the requested id verbatim (`magpie knows no model "auto/deepseek-v4.1-flash"`), same as the `nosuchgroup/foo` path, or
- name the real problem: `"auto" is not a routing group; auto groups are named auto/<model> (e.g. auto/step-5-preview)`, or
- list the members of the auto group it matched instead of global-catalog suggestions.

### Why it matters

A client integration that logs the error string will search for `group/auto-deepseek-v4-1-flash`, find nothing, and conclude the router is broken rather than the model name is wrong. I lost time on exactly this: the real cause was a model id from a different namespace, but the message pointed at an id that does not exist. Echoing the requested string (or saying which group was matched and what it contains) would have made it a one-line fix.

Minor, unrelated: `{"model":"workbuddy-ai/nope"}` returns `400 WorkBuddy AI: model [nope] service info not found` while other unknown models return 404 — upstream pass-through, mentioning only in case 400 vs 404 matters to clients' retry logic.

comments.body:
I ran into this too and put a fix together: the sent id is kept on the request context across `validateModel`'s canonicalization, and `unknownModel` (chat and embeddings) names it instead of the internal `group/auto-<slug>`; routing and the usage log still see the canonical id. Test included (`TestUnknownModelNamesTheSentID`).

The repo isn't open to pull requests from non-collaborators, so the change sits on a branch in my fork if you want to look or pull it in: https://github.com/tahodev/magpie/tree/fix-3150-sent-model-id (diff: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...tahodev:fix-3150-sent-model-id)

修了（按你提的第一种期望：逐字回显请求里的 id），在分支 [skygunner:fix/unknown-model-sent-id](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/unknown-model-sent-id)（commit 94861cc，基于 main 87d703c5）。README 说本仓库不开 PR，放在这里供取用。

改法：

- `requestModel` 现在把客户端原始发送的 model 一并返回；主入口（`s.handle`）、Gemini 的 `/v1beta/models/...`、Codex backend 的 `/backend-api/codex/responses` 三处入口在 id 被改写（`auto/<model>` → `group/auto-<slug>`）时用 `keepSentModel` 把原值挂在 request context 上（和 `subagentPickKey` 同款先例）。
- 404 站点优先用发送的 id：`auto/deepseek-v4.1-flash` 的拒绝消息现在报 `magpie knows no model "auto/deepseek-v4.1-flash"`，did-you-mean 建议也按原 id 计算（更贴合客户端视角）；`nosuchgroup/foo` 等本就原样回显的路径不变。
- 合成 id 无法从 `group/auto-<slug>` 反推（点号已丢），所以走的是保留原值而不是反向转换。

**验证**（`GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8`、`umask 022`；commit body 有完整记录）

- 新增 `TestUnknownModelNamesTheIdSent`：改动前红——正是你表格第一行（`auto/deepseek-v4.1-flash` → 报 `group/auto-deepseek-v4-1-flash`）；改动后绿——原 id 被点名、合成 id 不再出现、建议仍在、`nosuchgroup/foo` 依旧逐字回显。
- 其余 unknown-model 测试与 internal/gateway 包通过（包内仅有的红是 #3280，main 即红）；三平台 vet/build 通过；全量 `go test -tags nogui ./...` 67 ok，除 main 既有两红（#2207、#3280）外无新增。

顺带一提你文末那个 400/404 不一致（`workbuddy-ai/nope` 上游 400 直传）是另一件事，没动。

issue.title: [feat] allow disabling the stand-in for unserved models (fail with 404 instead of substituting)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

Please add a way to turn off magpie's stand-in for an unserved model, so the request fails with the existing 404 instead of being silently served by another model.

Today, when an agent asks for a model magpie doesn't serve, `serve` calls `standIn()` and, if the agent's config names a model, the request is answered by that model. The Routing log records `"moved": {"to": "...", "why": "stand-in"}`, but the agent gets a normal 200. There is no setting to opt out.

## Why this matters

1. **Silent substitution spends quota on a model the user did not pick.** The agent sees a normal reply; the only trace is the Routing page tag and the routing log.
2. **A stale thread model is the common trigger.** A Codex thread keeps the model id it was created with. If that provider/model is removed or renamed, every later turn in the thread is stood in, potentially for days, and nothing tells the user.
3. **The stand-in can cross configurations.** On Windows, if the Windows Codex config uses `openai_base_url` and has no `model_provider = "magpie"`, `codexStandIn()` returns empty, and `StandIn()` falls through to `wslCodexStandIn()`, which reads a running WSL distro's Codex config. A request from Windows Codex can therefore be answered by a model configured in a different OS's Codex.
4. **It is useful for magpie's own/agent auxiliary calls.** `codex-auto-review` and memory calls rely on a stand-in; an opt-out should not remove that, or should be scoped to user turns.

## Environment

- Windows 11, magpie `0.1.2777`
- Codex desktop, Windows `~/.codex/config.toml` has:
  - `openai_base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/backend-api/codex"`
  - no `model_provider`
- A running WSL Ubuntu Codex has `model_provider = "magpie"` and `model = "codex/gpt-6.1-terra"`

## What happened

1. A Codex thread was created while a provider with a URL-derived id existed; its stored model is `<provider-id>/glm-5-3-flash-260828`.
2. The provider was removed. The id is no longer in the catalog.
3. Every turn in that thread still sends `<provider-id>/glm-5-3-flash-260828`.
4. magpie's routing log shows:

   ```json
   "model": "<provider-id>/glm-5-3-flash-260828",
   "moved": { "to": "codex/gpt-6.1-terra", "why": "stand-in" }
   ```

   and the request is a 200, served by `gpt-6.1-terra`.
5. The Windows config alone yields no stand-in (`codexStandIn` requires `model_provider = "magpie"`), so `StandIn` falls through to `wslCodexStandIn()` and uses the WSL Ubuntu Codex's `model`.

The last point is especially surprising: a request from the Windows Codex is answered by the model in a different OS's Codex config, with no error and no visible warning in the agent.

## Expected

A setting to choose the behavior when a model is not served. Any of these shapes is fine:

- per agent: `magpie codex standin off` / a Settings switch
- per gateway key: `standIn=off`
- global: "When a model isn't served: stand in / fail"

When off:

- return the existing `unknownModel` 404 with the nearest ids, or
- keep the stand-in only for magpie's/agent auxiliary calls (`codex-auto-review`, memory) and fail user turns.

The default should stay as today to avoid breaking existing setups.

## Code

- `internal/gateway/gateway.go`: `movedStandIn`, `standIn()`
- `internal/agent/claude.go`: `StandIn()`
- `internal/agent/codex.go`: `codexStandIn()`
- `internal/agent/wsl.go`: `wslCodexStandIn()`

## Related

- #4864: a dropped model id leaves existing Codex threads unsendable (wants the opposite: keep old ids working)
- #2198: WSL Codex did not fall back to its own config model (the change that added `wslCodexStandIn`)
- #3150: 404 for an unknown `auto/...` model reports a synthesized id
- #742: unified purpose/routing/control for Codex auxiliary requests

I searched issues for `stand-in`, `standIn`, `顶替`, `unknown model`, `model_not_found`, `opt-out stand`, and `disable fallback model`, and found no request to disable the substitution itself.

issue.title: Provider headers: separate client identity policies for inference and Magpie-originated requests

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### Summary

Magpie currently uses different client identities for different requests to the
same provider, but its configuration does not model those request classes
separately.

For example, a key+URL provider can currently receive:

| Request class | Current default behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Agent inference | `User-Agent: magpie/<version>`, or the inbound Agent UA when `passUserAgent` applies |
| Model-list refresh | `User-Agent: magpie` |
| Provider/API test | No common default UA; special client headers may be added by the test path |
| Balance query | Usually no explicit UA, so the Go transport normally sends `Go-http-client/1.1` |
| Quota/usage query | Endpoint-specific headers; several paths also have no explicit UA |

Provider `Headers` can override defaults in several paths, but they are not
scoped by operation. `passUserAgent` addresses only part of the inference path.
As a result, one configured upstream can see unrelated Magpie identities, and
there is no explicit policy describing which identity each operation should
use.

### Why this matters

Some aggregators and relays distinguish supported clients through a coherent
set of headers such as `User-Agent`, `originator`, version, and other stable
client markers. Changing only the UA is not always sufficient and can produce
an internally inconsistent identity, as reported in
[#3851](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3851).

At the same time, Agent inference and Magpie-originated control requests are
not equivalent:

- an inference request may have a real initiating Agent identity to preserve;
- `model_list`, `provider_test`, `api_detect`, `balance`, and `quota_usage`
  are normally initiated by Magpie and may need a Magpie or provider-specific
  identity instead.

This is also difficult to diagnose today. The upstream-header visibility
requested by
[#2495](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/2495) and
[#3672](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3672) would show what was sent,
but configuration still needs to express what should be sent for each request
class.

### Proposed behavior

Allow each provider to select an independent header/client-identity policy for
at least:

- `inference`
- `model_list`
- `provider_test` / `api_detect`
- `balance`
- `quota_usage`

Possible policy sources:

- `magpie`: a consistent Magpie product identity;
- `agent_passthrough`: preserve the initiating Agent identity when one exists;
- `client_profile:<name>`: use a named, coherent client profile;
- `custom`: use request-class-specific custom headers.

`agent_passthrough` should not silently apply to a background request with no
initiating Agent.

A client profile should be a coherent set rather than a UA string alone.
Stable identity/capability headers may belong in a profile, while
authentication, cookies, attestations, request IDs, and per-request
session/thread/turn values must remain dynamic and outside static profiles.

The existing provider-wide `Headers` behavior can remain as the backward
compatible fallback. A request-class override should take precedence, and the
scrubbed traces proposed in #2495/#3672 should show the selected policy and the
effective final headers.

### Observable boundary

For a relay-backed provider there may be four parties:

1. Agent
2. Magpie
3. Configured upstream/relay
4. Final model vendor behind the relay

Magpie can observe the headers it receives from the Agent, sends to the
configured upstream, receives from that upstream, and returns to the Agent. It
cannot observe or prove the relay-internal `3 -> 4` headers unless the relay
reports them, so that hop should remain explicitly opaque.

### Security and non-goals

- Never expose values for authorization, API keys, cookies, access/refresh
  tokens, signatures, or attestations in traces or telemetry.
- Do not copy per-request identity or authentication material into reusable
  profiles.
- Do not present a named client profile as a way to bypass provider
  restrictions. Header similarity does not guarantee acceptance and may be
  incompatible with a provider's policy.
- Remotely updated profiles, if wanted later, should be a separate opt-in,
  versioned, reviewable design rather than silently changing existing
  providers.

### Acceptance criteria

- One provider can use Agent identity for inference and Magpie/custom identity
  for model-list, test, balance, and quota requests.
- The actual selected policy and final scrubbed UA/header names are visible per
  outbound attempt through the work in #2495/#3672.
- A custom `User-Agent` override has visible provenance.
- Retries and fallbacks retain separate sanitized snapshots.
- Secret values never appear.
- Relay-internal `3 -> 4` headers are marked unavailable rather than inferred.

<details>
<summary>Current source references</summary>

Reviewed on current `main` at
[`7e0fe83d`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/commit/7e0fe83d4b8f58a6a69c8d4876ef3b08d312744a)
on October 31, 2026.

- Inference UA selection:
  [`internal/gateway/user_agent.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/7e0fe83d4b8f58a6a69c8d4876ef3b08d312744a/internal/gateway/user_agent.go#L11-L27)
- Inference headers and signing:
  [`internal/gateway/gateway.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/7e0fe83d4b8f58a6a69c8d4876ef3b08d312744a/internal/gateway/gateway.go#L4613-L4719)
- Model-list headers:
  [`internal/catalog/live.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/7e0fe83d4b8f58a6a69c8d4876ef3b08d312744a/internal/catalog/live.go#L517-L540)
- Balance request:
  [`internal/provider/balance.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/7e0fe83d4b8f58a6a69c8d4876ef3b08d312744a/internal/provider/balance.go#L1241-L1263)
- Quota request example:
  [`internal/provider/planquota.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/7e0fe83d4b8f58a6a69c8d4876ef3b08d312744a/internal/provider/planquota.go#L593-L608)
- Provider test path:
  [`internal/provider/test.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/7e0fe83d4b8f58a6a69c8d4876ef3b08d312744a/internal/provider/test.go#L675-L710)
- Existing Test-as-client profiles:
  [`internal/provider/test_as.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/7e0fe83d4b8f58a6a69c8d4876ef3b08d312744a/internal/provider/test_as.go#L15-L37)

</details>

  request/response headers through OTLP
- [#1851](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/1851) — optional inbound
  Agent UA pass-through
- [#2817](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/2817) and
  [#4197](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/4197) — missing Claude

- [#3052](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3052) — an Agent header
